title: Add chainable-session snapshot quickstart with deterministic replay and contract linter
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: debugging multi-turn RAG flows and reproducing regressions is hard without compact, versioned checkpoints. This quickstart introduces a chainable snapshot format and a tiny replay harness that makes deterministic debugging and contract checks trivial for engineers.

Summary: adds a new quickstart `rag-chain-snapshot` that demonstrates: 1) chainable session snapshots (versioned, minimal payloads capturing retrieval deltas, model token diffs, and tool-call envelopes); 2) a schema-enforced structured-output contract for tool calls and step records; 3) a deterministic replay runner that can pin a model variant or run against a local mock and performs token-precise diffs; 4) a devcontainer for reproducible local testing and a console-friendly telemetry probe that emits span-like events to stdout.

Highlights and rationale: The snapshot format is intentionally compact to encourage frequent checkpoints during iterative authoring. Each snapshot contains metadata (version, quickstart, seed), a `steps` array with `user`, `retrieval`, `model`, and `tools` subsections, and optional annotations for manually marking interesting frames. The replay harness validates the JSON Schema, replays prompts to a pinned model-id (or a stubbed mock) and reports regressions with a concise diff. This approach helps support teams reproduce SUP tickets and enables maintainers to run contract checks in CI.

How to try locally: copy .env.example to .env and add REDWOOD_API_KEY, start the devcontainer or run `docker compose up --build`, then `npm run dev` to open the small playground. Use `npm run record-session -- --example=payment-refund` to produce a snapshot in ./snapshots and `npm run replay -- --file=snapshots/payment-refund-1.json` to replay and run the contract linter.

CI: added a Jest-based smoke test that synthesizes a snapshot and runs the contract linter. A flake was observed on first run due to mock timing; I implemented a lightweight retry (3 attempts) around the mock server startup to stabilize CI. All checks are now passing.

Security/PII: quickstart purposely avoids shipping any real customer data. The SQLite seed is synthetic and the seeded DB is added to .gitignore if generated locally. No keys are committed.

Review notes: reviewers asked to keep the snapshot schema extensible (versioned) and to avoid heavy deps. I kept the runtime minimal (Node 18+, tiny dev UI) and added a clear migration path in docs.

Merge: squash-and-merge to keep the quickstart changes atomic.

Planned follow-ups: wire telemetry probe to Redwood Console exporter, contribute schema to redwood-model-registry, add a typed SDK helper in redwood-sdk-typescript to read/write snapshots.
commits: implement replay runner and token diffing
fix flaky mock startup with retry
review_comments: Liam Chen: Can we keep the schema backward-compatible? — Answer: added version field and migration notes in README.
Maya Rodriguez: Please avoid heavy runtime deps in the quickstart UI. — Answer: replaced heavyweight UI library with a minimal web component and inlined CSS.
Thomas Nguyen: CI flaked on mock server startup. — Action: added a retry loop and a short backoff; observed stability after change.
release_notes: Add chainable-session snapshot quickstart: provides deterministic replay, schema-based contract linter, and devcontainer for reproducible debugging.
note_to_ops: This quickstart is demo-only; if you wire telemetry to Redwood Console later, ensure sample traces are tagged with quickstart:rag-chain-snapshot to avoid confusion with production traces.
